sections.hypothesis: On ETH and SOL 5m, a failed breakdown below the previous UTC day's value area, reclaimed by a bar where buyers took most of the volume, gives long trades back toward the point of control that beat random entries with the same stops, targets and sizing, and beat holding at the same exposure on Sharpe, after costs.
sections.rationale: Who pays, as the method claims (Fabio Valentino, Luke's YouTube batch 2 C): sellers who pushed price out of the accepted range are trapped when it is reclaimed, and their stops and covering push price back to where most volume traded. Order flow is a new family for Kestrel (not pullbacks or patterns), but it is a minute-chart method. Its own cost gate (2026-11-16, stops only, not a trial, 5m 2020-25) put ETH and SOL at all hours at MARGINAL (median 0.36R and 0.26R of costs a trade) and BTC at FAILS (0.53R), so BTC is left out (chosen on cost, never outcomes). The point of control sits a median 1.5R away, so the break-even win rate after costs is about 51-55%. Delta here is each bar's taker-buy share (Binance's own split), a stand-in for trade-level data. Luke chose to test it knowingly (2026-11-16).
sections.rules: order-flow, ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT 5m separately, spot, long only. Each UTC day: the previous day's volume profile (each 5m bar's volume at its typical price, bins of 5 bps of the last close); point of control = the busiest bin; value area = 70% of the volume grown from it. The first bar of the day whose low is below the value area low starts a breakdown; within 15 bars of it, a bar closing above the value area low with taker buys above half its volume is the signal. Entry at the next bar's open; stop at the lowest low from the breakdown bar to the signal; target the point of control (it must be above the signal close). One setup a day. A trade still open is sold at the next open after the day's last bar (the first open of the next UTC day: an intraday method); a signal on the day's last bar is skipped. A day whose previous day has no bars has no setup. Costs from kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fee a side, 1 bp half-spread: a 17 bps round trip), 330 USDT, 1% risk per trade sized by the engine, capped at 100% of equity. Period 2020-01 (SOL 2020-08) to 2025-10, before the holdout.
sections.falsification: The full scorecard on each coin, including test 9: net expectancy per trade must beat 95% of 200 random-entry paths with the same stops, targets and sizing (kestrel random-entry). Fails if neither coin passes every test.
sections.parameters: bin_bps 5 (2-20), value_area_pct 70 (60-80), reclaim_bars 15 (5-30). One setting on each coin: 2 runs; the robustness check moves each (about 15 neighbours a coin).
sections.costs: At most one trade a day, perhaps 100-150 a year a coin (the gate found about 120-130 setups a year at all hours). At about 0.4R of costs a trade and a target under 2R, costs are the main obstacle; the random-entry control shows whether anything beats them. Trials: 2 runs plus about 30 neighbours; random-entry paths aren't trials.
